nodes.summary: BALANCED BICLIQUE is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ that is well formed (the entries of $es$ are distinct, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ has $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \neq v$ and $(v, u) \notin es$) and for which there are disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ of exactly $K$ vertices each in…
nodes.title: The decision problem BALANCED BICLIQUE

nodes.summary: A balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is feasible when there are disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ of exactly $K$ vertices each in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, where distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $es$. In other words, the graph contains a complete bipartite subgraph $K_{K,K}$, not necessarily induced.
nodes.title: Feasible balanced biclique instances

nodes.summary: An instance of BALANCED BICLIQUE is a triple $(n, es, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: Balanced biclique instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem BALANCED BICLIQUE belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: BALANCED BICLIQUE is NP-complete

nodes.summary: The graph of a balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $es$.
nodes.title: Graph of a balanced biclique instance

nodes.summary: A balanced biclique instance $(n, es, K)$ is well formed when the entries of the list $es$ are distinct and every pair $(u, v)$ in $es$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \neq v$ and $(v, u) \notin es$.
nodes.title: Well-formed balanced biclique instances
